clue.text: Upset about wine, it gets sent back in place of posh nosh

indicators.note: being sent back means the whole assembly is read from its end to its start
about means going round, so the word for upset surrounds the next two pieces

parts.note: to bug someone is to upset or annoy them
port is a fortified wine from Portugal
it, as in sex appeal, is abbreviated SA in crosswords

explanation.surface: A diner, upset about the wine, sends it back at a smart restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the diner's mood but is the bug; 'it gets sent back' looks like the wine but reverses the whole assembly, BUPORTSAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a British pub serving restaurant-quality food, so it is a place for upmarket cooking.

clue.text: One getting into mature woman a little bit

indicators.note: getting into means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, an older woman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone gets a little bit into a mature woman's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a tiny particle or small amount, as in a grain of truth.

clue.text: Tree-hugging monkey missing an Eastern dish

indicators.note: hugging means the monkey word wraps around the tree
missing tells us the word an is dropped

parts.note: simian means a monkey or ape
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree-hugging monkey goes without an Eastern dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-hugging' reads as eco-friendly, but it is ASH held inside SIMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is a Japanese dish of thin slices of raw fish.

clue.text: Cross road, avoiding the Tibetan yak heads

indicators.note: heads are the front ends, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Crossing a road to avoid Tibetan yaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb for the road but is the adjective, meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Seer gains by speaking aloud

indicators.note: speaking aloud signals the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: profit means gains or earnings

explanation.surface: A seer earns money by public speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet is someone who foretells the future, which a seer does.

clue.text: Revel?

parts.note: the word read backwards is lever, which is a pedal-like control, so it is a pedal turned back

explanation.surface: A one-word question about partying.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put a pedal (lever) back, and lever reversed makes the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to retreat from a position, and literally a pedal worked in reverse gives the clue.

clue.text: Reportedly filthy bird

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: foul means filthy or disgusting

explanation.surface: A dirty bird, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowl is a bird, especially a domestic one such as a chicken.

clue.text: Very great friend so wounded for the last time?

definitions.text: so wounded for the last time?

parts.note: fat means large, as in a fat cheque
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A very great friend has been wounded for the final time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal wound is one described with this adverb, ending a life, so the last wound anyone receives.

clue.text: Something for sharpening false teeth, shown leaving hospital

indicators.note: false means not genuine, signalling the letters are rearranged
leaving tells us a letter is to be removed from the pool

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: False teeth are shown to someone leaving hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: TEETH plus SHOWN less H gives TEETHSOWN, rearranged by 'false'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone is a stone used for honing the edge of blades.

clue.text: Lofty range of latest shifts

indicators.note: shifts tells us the letters of the words before it are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: The highest vocal range of the latest work shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like a noun (work shifts) but is the anagram signal on OF LATEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a singer's high voice register above the normal range, hence a lofty range.

clue.text: Censorship?

parts.note: read as censor's ship: a censor is one who cuts material

explanation.surface: A one-word question about suppressing published material.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as censor + ship: the vessel belonging to a censor.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor removes scenes, so is one who cuts, and a cutter is also a single-masted boat.

clue.text: Something, nothing less — not yet, I suspect

indicators.note: less tells us a piece is to be taken away from the letters being rearranged
suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious, signals that the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: nothing is zero, represented by the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone muses that something is not quite there yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from the letters of NOT YET I and rearrange the remaining NTYETI.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is any thing that has its own existence, so it can stand for something.

clue.text: Desperate when out of bounds to secure birdie, ultimately

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the first piece holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: bounds are hops, and being out of them is being hop-less

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A golfer is desperate because a ball out of bounds wrecks the chance of a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' is read as 'without hops', HOP + LESS, not as a golf penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeless and desperate are synonyms, both describing a situation beyond rescue.

clue.text: Archer committing perjury, still held in secure place — or not?

definitions.text: Archer committing perjury, still held in secure place — or not?

indicators.note: held in means the following pieces are placed inside the stronghold word
not, after or, says those two letters are to be dropped

parts.note: a fortress is a secure, fortified place
Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and peer, was jailed for perjury, that is for telling lies
still can mean nevertheless, as but does

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, convicted of perjury, is still held in prison, or is he?
explanation.walkthrough: FORTRESS without OR is FTRESS, which holds LYING and BUT. Jeffrey Archer is a British novelist and politician jailed for perjury in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress of the arching kind is a support propping a wall from outside, which secures a building yet does not fully touch it.

clue.text: Praising old racing driver, politician

parts.note: Niki Lauda was an Austrian Formula One champion of the 1970s and 1980s
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An old racing driver turned politician gets praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means expressing praise, an adjective from the Latin for praise.

clue.text: Dog in stormy tea garden

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of the words that follow are churned

explanation.surface: A dog is out in a tea garden during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

clue.text: Play written around current book showing youth in the '50s

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the following ones

parts.note: to toy is to play with something
an eddy is a swirling current of water

explanation.surface: A play has been written about a contemporary book that shows the life of a 1950s youth.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a British youth of the 1950s known for Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy boys were young men of 1950s Britain, a youth subculture with drape jackets and quiffs.

clue.text: See 12
Tea garden's last storm

parts.note: Typhoo is a British brand of tea

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The last storm in the tea garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Typhoo is a well-known British tea brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone in the western Pacific, a violent storm.

clue.text: Model secured for lothario

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A model was secured as a lothario's latest conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a womaniser, after a rake in an 18th-century play, so a man who seduces.

clue.text: One designed to climb — or run

definitions.meaning: a framework of rungs built for climbing up
a run in tights or stockings is a line of unravelled stitches, called this in Britain

explanation.surface: Something built for climbing, or for running.
explanation.definitionFit: The rung-frame for climbing and the British word for a stocking run share this spelling.

clue.text: See 22 across
Covered with woven material, wigged

definitions.meaning: laid with a floor covering of woven fabric
to wig someone is old slang for scolding them, and being called in for a scolding is this word too

explanation.surface: Something covered with woven fabric, and also wearing a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wigged' looks like wearing a wig but here means rebuked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having a floor covering and, informally in Britain, being reprimanded by a superior.

clue.text: Nevadan died in Montana, dog buried there

indicators.note: buried there means the letters lie concealed inside the words just given

explanation.surface: A man from Nevada died in Montana and his dog was buried there with him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dandie Dinmont is a Scottish terrier breed, named after a character in a Walter Scott novel.

clue.text: Ultimately, rude crossword turned this air blue?

indicators.note: turned means the assembled letters are read backwards
ultimately points to the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: a crossword is a grid of squares

explanation.surface: A crude crossword made the solver turn the air blue with swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air blue' looks like swearing, but blue means sad and an air is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament, so a sad tune.

clue.text: Nation, I reckon, disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means the central letter, the heart, is removed

parts.note: to tally is to count up or reckon

explanation.surface: Someone reckons the nation is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Country reflected in outskirts of Brasilia, South American capital

indicators.note: in means the reversed country sits inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are taken
reflected means the word for the country is read backwards as in a mirror

parts.note: Togo is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A country seen reflected on the edge of Brasilia, a South American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasilia looks like the definition but is only the source of B and A; OGOT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital city of Colombia in South America.

clue.text: Rank expert back in the pink

indicators.note: in tells us the turned expert goes inside the colour word

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour

indicators.note: back means the word for expert is read in reverse

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional

explanation.surface: An expert at rank returns in the pink of health.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a rank in the army, a junior non-commissioned officer.

clue.text: Colour yellow primarily recorded on film?

indicators.note: something recorded on film is said to be in the can, so the letter goes inside the film container

parts.note: film is stored in a can, a round metal case

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A colour of yellow mainly captured on film.
explanation.walkthrough: Film shot and finished is 'in the can', so Y goes into CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries.

clue.text: Seriously old walls in home

indicators.note: to wall in is to enclose, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: early can mean old or ancient, as in early times
a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: An old house really does have walls inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly and seriously are synonyms, both meaning with sincere intent.
